memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said." - Exodus 8:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the most searching verses in the whole book. When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his heart.

Not when the pressure increased — when it eased. Prosperity undid what pain had begun.

Many of us know this pattern from the inside. In a crisis we pray desperately, read the Bible daily, cry out to God. Then the diagnosis comes back clear, the job comes through, the child recovers — and within weeks the fervour is gone.

Relief exposed what the crisis had hidden: Pharaoh never wanted God. He only wanted his frogs gone.

This is why Scripture warns so often about comfortable seasons. Moses would later warn Israel that when they were full and settled, they must be careful not to forget the Lord (Deut 8:11-14). Ease is spiritually more dangerous than hardship.

If God has recently given you relief, that is a mercy — but it is also a test. What will you do with the answered prayer?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has my prayer life weakened since God answered my last big request?
2. Am I more faithful to God in crisis than in comfort?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me close to You in easy seasons as well as hard ones. Do not let relief make me careless. Amen.
